topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the opening framing, introducing the lecturer and the core learning outcomes of the lecture.

topics.label: Concepts of cancer etiology, inherited predisposition, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental balance between intrinsic genetic processes, bad luck, and environmental exposures in driving cancer development, supported by global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how biological pathogens drive malignant transformation through mechanisms such as chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and direct cellular disruption.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation and chemical compounds undergo xenobiotic metabolism to form DNA adducts and drive genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and mechanistic principles
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic promoter activity, developmental windows of vulnerability, and the multi-step nature of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the experimental, analytical, and epidemiological approaches used to prove carcinogenicity alongside the evaluation of human exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with closing framing and high-level takeaway points.
